structured.approach: I followed DE-06 in the data-engineering-steps skill. I read both contracted inputs with context_get to get receipts: feat.data_model_change at 3943254 and org.customer_mappings at e8afce8. As background I read the approved feat.design (722a98f) for B1.2, B1.4, B1.5, DC-1, DC-2, DD-6 and DD-7. The ap_pipeline code and tests came from the step's tool view, and I read data/sample_feed.csv from the checkout. Where feat.mappings names a later step, I cite the skill file that defines it: DE-07 and DE-08 read feat.mappings, DE-09 writes the unit tests, and DE-13 schedules from org.customer_mappings. I compared the latest customer contract (feed v3 columns, paid_date -> Invoice.paid_date, schedule) with the Data Model change field by field. From that I wrote feat.mappings in full. It contains the source-to-target mapping, the ordered transformation steps, the derived Delay-history mapping, the schedule mapping, synthetic validation cases and open questions. Mapping is a documentation step and coding is DE-08, so I changed no code. I ran the repository CI to confirm the baseline still passes, and git status shows a clean working tree.

claims.text: The latest customer contract lists vendor feed v3 columns invoice_id, vendor, due_date, amount, paid, paid_date, with paid_date optional, an ISO date and empty when unpaid, and maps paid_date -> Invoice.paid_date.
The customer contract agrees with the Data Model change: Invoice gains paid_date (date or None) from feed v3, and feed v2 must keep loading.

The existing column mappings stay as they are: invoice_id -> id (strip), vendor -> vendor (strip), due_date -> due_date (date.fromisoformat), amount -> amount (Decimal), paid -> paid ('true' after strip/lower, missing means false).

The paid_date rule: a missing column, None or blank gives None. Otherwise the stripped value is parsed with date.fromisoformat. A non-blank invalid value rejects the row with reason 'paid_date'. This check runs only after the existing fields pass.

The Delay history includes only paid records with a paid_date, with delay_days = (paid_date - due_date).days in calendar days. Values are in feed order and negative values are kept. It is in memory only and is consumed by ap_forecast vendor_risk.
The customer schedule (daily 02:00 Asia/Kolkata, unchanged) matches schedule.json (frequency daily, time 02:00, timezone Asia/Kolkata).

DE-07 reads feat.mappings with task.components, DE-08 Coding reads feat.mappings, DE-09 writes the unit tests for the transformation logic, and DE-13 schedules the pipelines from org.customer_mappings.
The repository sample feed still uses the v2 header invoice_id,vendor,due_date,amount,paid, so the v3 cases need synthetic test rows.
This step changes no code: transform.py does not yet map paid_date and there is no delays.py module. TSK-01 and TSK-02 implement the mapping in DE-08.
Monetary amounts stay Decimal, never float, and delays use calendar days.

open_questions: MQ-1 (non-blocking, Data modeler): the customer contract now names the v3 column paid_date. Can CQ-DE4-4 (no v3 specification in the inputs) be closed?

MQ-2 (non-blocking, Product manager / feed owner): the contract says paid_date is 'empty when unpaid', but the model accepts an unpaid row with a valid paid_date and keeps the date (DD-7, OQ-B6). Should such a row be rejected, or its date cleared, instead?

MQ-3 (non-blocking, Data engineering lead / Product manager): the contract gives no effective date for feed v3, and CQ-DE4-1 is still open. Must v2 and v3 feeds load side by side? Interim: yes, a missing column gives None.

MQ-4 (non-blocking, Data modeler): is a paid_date cell holding only whitespace treated as blank (None) or as invalid (reject)? Interim: blank, because the value is stripped first. To be confirmed in a unit test.
Carried DMQ-1, DMQ-2 and DMQ-3 from feat.data_model_change are unchanged.
structured.summary: I wrote feat.mappings.md in full. Pulling in the latest customer contract (feed v3) adds one mapping, paid_date -> Invoice.paid_date, and the contract agrees with the Data Model change on every field. The existing column mappings are unchanged. The file sets out the transformation steps in order: existing fields first, then paid_date, with reject reason 'paid_date'. It also covers the derived Delay-history mapping, the schedule check (daily 02:00 Asia/Kolkata, matching schedule.json) and synthetic validation cases for coding and unit tests. References to later steps now cite the data-engineering-steps skill file. No code was changed, CI passes on the baseline and the working tree is clean. There are four non-blocking questions (MQ-1 to MQ-4) and no blocking ones.
